# Test coverage additions for tests/test_rbtree.c

## Context
A read-through of `tests/test_rbtree.c` against the contract in `include/rbtree.h`
found six coverage gaps: (1) nothing proves `rb_insert` copies the key rather than
aliasing the caller's buffer, (2) nothing proves `rb_destroy` runs `value_free` on
every value still live in a non-empty tree, (3) the rebalancing tests never call
`rb_find` after the rotations they trigger, (4) `rb_foreach`'s tests ignore the
`value` argument entirely, (5) the only rebalancing inputs are a pure ascending and
a pure descending run, which in a standard RB-insert-fixup only ever drives
straight-line (LL/RR) rotations — the zig-zag (LR/RL) double-rotation branch is
never exercised, and (6) `rb_validate`'s fixtures cover BST order, red-red, and
black-height, but never isolate "root must be black." This plan closes all six,
reworking existing cases where they already cover most of the ground and adding
new cases only where the scenario is genuinely new (the zig-zag/mixed-order
inserts, and the root-red fixture). Per your direction, cases 7/8 are edited by
appending checks, not restructured into a shared helper, and no case is deleted.

All changes are confined to `tests/test_rbtree.c`. Nothing in `include/rbtree.h`
or `src/rbtree.c` is touched (src is still hand-written stubs per the existing
TODOs, so `make test`/`asan`/`memcheck` are expected to keep failing there until
`rb_create` follow-ups implement `rb_insert`/`rb_find`/`rb_foreach`/`rb_validate` —
that's unchanged by this plan and not a regression to fix here).

## Changes

### 1. Key-copy ownership — rework `insert_distinct_keys_accumulates_size` (case 6, ~line 439)
Switch the three literal keys to local mutable buffers, insert as today, then
mutate each buffer's contents *after* the insert call returns, before the
existing `rb_find`/`rb_size` assertions:

```c
char buf_a[] = "a-key", buf_m[] = "m-key", buf_z[] = "z-key";
assert(rb_insert(t, buf_a, "a-value") == 0);
assert(rb_insert(t, buf_m, "m-value") == 0);
assert(rb_insert(t, buf_z, "z-value") == 0);

memset(buf_a, 'X', strlen(buf_a));
memset(buf_m, 'X', strlen(buf_m));
memset(buf_z, 'X', strlen(buf_z));
```

Keep the existing `rb_size`/`rb_find` assertions unchanged (they already check
`"a-key"`, `"m-key"`, `"z-key"` by fresh literal content, so they now double as
the ownership check), and add one new assertion that a mutated buffer's content
finds nothing: `assert(rb_find(t, "XXXXX") == NULL);`. If `rb_insert` stored the
caller's pointer instead of a `rb_malloc`+`memcpy` copy, the mutated buffer would
either break the existing lookups or make `"XXXXX"` resolve — either way this
case starts failing. Rename the case's `printf` label to
`insert_distinct_keys_prove_key_copy` to reflect the added purpose.

### 2. `rb_destroy` value ownership — rework case 5 (`insert_overwrite_frees_old_value`, ~line 411)
This case already tracks `old_value`/`new_value` via `track_free` and destroys
the tree at the end, but never checks that `new_value` (still live in the tree
at destroy time) actually gets freed. Two edits:
- Insert two more distinct keys with their own tracked heap values before the
  `rb_destroy(t)` call, so the destroy has to walk multiple surviving nodes, not
  just one.
- Add assertions right after `rb_destroy(t)` that every surviving value was
  freed exactly once (via the existing `was_freed`/`freed_count` machinery).

```c
char *extra1 = malloc(8); strcpy(extra1, "extra1");
char *extra2 = malloc(8); strcpy(extra2, "extra2");
assert(rb_insert(t, "extra-key-1", extra1) == 0);
assert(rb_insert(t, "extra-key-2", extra2) == 0);

rb_destroy(t);
assert(was_freed(new_value));
assert(was_freed(extra1));
assert(was_freed(extra2));
assert(freed_count == 4); /* old_value (overwrite) + new_value, extra1, extra2 (destroy) */
```

### 3 & 4. Find-after-rebalance and foreach value checks — append to cases 7 & 8 (~lines 458-509)
Two small additions to each of `insert_rebalances_ascending_run` and
`insert_rebalances_descending_run`, done in place (no restructuring):

- Extend `collect_ctx_t` (~line 66) with a parallel `values[MAX_COLLECT]` array,
  and `collect_cb` (~line 71) to record `value` alongside `key`.
- In each of cases 7/8, after the existing sorted-order `strcmp` loop, add a
  pointer-equality check that the value collected at each position matches the
  value that was actually inserted for that key: for the ascending case,
  `collected.values[i] == (void *)keys[i]`; for the descending case (whose
  sorted order is the reverse of its insertion array),
  `collected.values[i] == (void *)keys[run_len - 1 - i]`.
- After the existing `rb_foreach` block and before `rb_destroy(t)`, add a loop
  asserting `rb_find(t, keys[i]) == (void *)keys[i]` for every `i` in the run,
  so every key is independently confirmed reachable by search (not just by
  in-order walk) after the rotations the run triggers.

### 5. Zig-zag and mixed-order rebalancing — three new cases, same style as 7/8
Added directly after case 8, following its existing shape (create tree, insert
loop with size checks, `rb_validate`, `rb_foreach` + value checks, per-key
`rb_find` checks, destroy). Hand-verified insertion/expected-sorted pairs:

- **Case 9 — LR zig-zag**: insert `{"c", "a", "b"}`. Trace: `c` becomes root
  (black); `a` inserted red as `c`'s left child (parent is root, fixup loop
  doesn't run); `b` inserted red as `a`'s right child — `a` is red and is
  `c`'s *left* child while `b` is `a`'s *right* child, the mismatched
  case that forces a left-rotation at `a` followed by a right-rotation at `c`
  (a genuine double rotation, not two single ones). Sorted order:
  `{"a", "b", "c"}`.
- **Case 10 — RL zig-zag**: insert `{"a", "c", "b"}`. Mirror trace: `a` root,
  `c` red right child, `b` inserted red as `c`'s left child — `c` is `a`'s
  *right* child while `b` is `c`'s *left* child, forcing a right-rotation at
  `c` then a left-rotation at `a`. Sorted order: `{"a", "b", "c"}`.
- **Case 11 — mixed/random order**: insert
  `{"m","f","t","d","h","p","b","e","g","s","v"}` (11 keys, non-monotonic,
  forces a mix of recolors and rotations on both sides of the tree). Sorted
  order: `{"b","d","e","f","g","h","m","p","s","t","v"}`.

Each case is a standalone block (like cases 7/8 today), not a shared helper,
per your preference — some duplication of the check shape is accepted in
exchange for keeping cases 7/8 edited by pure append rather than restructured.

### 6. Root-must-be-black — new fixture in `test_rb_validate` (~end of the file's validate cases, after line 342)
Add one case isolating the fourth invariant, following the existing
`mk_node`-based fixture style: a single-node tree whose root is `RB_RED` with
both children `t->nil`. This trivially satisfies BST order (one node), red-red
(no children to violate it with), and black-height (both root-to-nil paths are
length 0/equal) — the only broken rule is root color.

```c
{
    rbtree_t *t = rb_create(NULL);
    assert(t);
    rbnode_t *root = mk_node(t, "m", RB_RED);
    root->left = root->right = t->nil;
    root->parent = t->nil;
    t->root = root;
    t->size = 1;
    assert(rb_validate(t) != 0);
    rb_destroy(t);
    printf("ok - validate_root_must_be_black\n");
}
```

Also update the descriptive comment above the invariant-isolation cases
(~lines 176-180), which currently says rb_validate's TODO "lists exactly three
invariants" — reword to four and mention the new root-color case, so the
comment stays accurate.

## Verification
- Read back the diff to confirm every new/changed block still follows the
  file's existing conventions (invariant comments on loops, `printf("ok - ...")`
  per case, fresh tree per case).
- Run `make test` (via the `battery` skill's sequence, or directly) to confirm
  the file still compiles cleanly under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` — expect
  assertion failures once execution reaches the still-stubbed `rb_insert` /
  `rb_find` / `rb_foreach` / `rb_validate`, consistent with the current state
  of the suite before this change. A full green run isn't expected until those
  functions are implemented; that's outside this plan's scope.

This is glibc's stdio internals, not your code. `printf`/`stdout` lazily allocates an internal output buffer the first time it's used (`_IO_file_doallocate` → `malloc`), and that buffer is only ever freed implicitly at process exit — nothing in `test_rbtree.c` owns or is expected to free it. Valgrind reports it as "still reachable" (the weakest leak category — it found a live pointer to the block at exit) rather than "definitely lost," which is exactly the signature of this kind of libc-internal allocation.

It won't fail `make memcheck`: `--error-exitcode=1` in the [Makefile:31-33](Makefile#L31-L33) only triggers on actual Valgrind errors, and by default "still reachable" blocks aren't counted as errors (Valgrind's default `--errors-for-leak-kinds` is `definite,possible`, not `reachable`). So this is just informational noise in the report, not a gating failure — nothing to fix here.
